Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Blora Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as the element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries and is authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Sub-district is a district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the duties of the district head.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, court, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of Victims of violence to be able to work and be self-sufficient after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any action against women that results or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is women and Children who experience violence and/or threat of violence within the scope of household and community.
14. Facilitator is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide handling and protection for Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that provides Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the district and village/sub-district level that provides protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from disturbance of psychosocial condition and restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and facing difficulties in legal matters outside or before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and their child, or mother and their child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relations due to blood relation, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Point a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, group, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, compatible and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances to access, participate, control and benefit from the implementation of development and enjoy the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Point e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death occurring during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions

Point f.

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g

What is meant by "respect for the opinion of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h

What is meant by "openness" is that the implementation of victim protection is transparent among integrated service providers.

Point i

What is meant by "integration" is that the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, religious leaders, social workers, police.

Point j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence they experienced.

Point k

What is meant by "empowering" is every effort provided must strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Point l

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of the victim to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection towards Victims includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts towards Victims of Violence.

Article 15

Paragraph (1)

Point a

Sufficiently clear.

Point b

Prevention efforts within the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening household resilience such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication among family members.

Point c

Prevention efforts within the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence occurring in their environment.

Point c

Educational institutions can participate in efforts to provide educational punishment, endeavoring to eliminate provisions that do not side with victims of violence.

Paragraph (2)

Point a

What is meant by "network" includes: family partners, dasawisma, family groups existing in the Region. Point b

What is meant by "coordination" includes: planning, implementation and monitoring of violence prevention programs. Point c

What is meant by "violence prevention system" includes: mapping locations or areas prone to violence and conducting promotive and preventive efforts to the community.

Point d

Socialization can be conducted through mass media, electronic media, and direct counseling to the community.

Article 27

(1) The Regent exercises control, guidance and supervision over the provision of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence at the regency and Village/Sub-district levels.

(2) In exercising control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may delegate to the Regional Apparatus responsible for the affairs of women's empowerment and Child protection.

Article 11

(1) In an effort to enhance protection for Victims of violence, UPPA is established at the sub-district and Village/Sub-district levels.

(2) UPPA at the sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by the Sub-district Head by involving community institutions, the Sub-district Level Family Welfare Development Task Force, community leaders and Child representatives.

(3) UPPA at the Village/Sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by the Village Head/Sub-district Head by involving Village/Sub-district officials, community institutions in the Village/Sub-district, the Family Welfare Development Task Force, community leaders and Child representatives.

(4) UPPA as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to provide protection to Victims in the form of:

a. pursuing prevention and handling;
b. conducting coordination in the framework of handling services for Victims of Violence;
c. pursuing increased community participation; and d. conducting monitoring and reporting.

Article 17

Point a

What is meant by "fast" is immediate action taken without complications or simplified procedures.

Point b

What is meant by "safe and comfortable" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, undisturbed, and served in a friendly, respectful and appreciative manner.

Point c

What is meant by "empathy" is an act of appreciating, respecting, caring, being friendly, and making happy with the aim of pleasing and calming the victim's heart.

Point d

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is service to women and children victims of violence without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point e

What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people regardless of their social status, so that such services are affordable for the underprivileged or relatively affordable for the privileged.

Point f

What is meant by "not subject to fees" is that service and assistance activities conducted by PPT are not charged to victims.

Point g

What is meant by "guaranteed confidentiality" is an effort to ensure certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.

CHAPTER VIII

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE Part One

General

Article 23

(1) Forms of fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Violence include the fulfillment of Children's basic rights according to their needs.

(2) The fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is the responsibility of the Regional Government, family, and community.

Article 30

(1) At the time this Regional Regulation comes into effect, the institution/network of Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence of Blora Regency and the Prevention and Handling Unit for Women and Children Victims of Violence in Villages/Sub-districts that have already been formed shall continue to carry out their duties until the establishment of the institution/network of Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence of Blora Regency and the Prevention and Handling Unit for Women and Children Victims of Violence in Villages/Sub-districts based on this Regional Regulation.

(2) The adjustment of the network institution of Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence of Blora Regency and the Prevention and Handling Unit for Women and Children Victims of Violence in Villages/Sub-districts shall be implemented no later than 1 (one) year.

Paragraph 1

Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

Article 14

The organization of protection for Victims of Violence is carried out through: a. prevention efforts;

b. services; and

c. empowerment.

8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of Victims of violence to be able to work and be self-sufficient after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any action against women that results or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Blora Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as the element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries and is authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Sub-district is a district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the duties of the district head.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, court, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of Victims of violence to be able to work and be self-sufficient after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any action against women that results or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is women and Children who experience violence and/or threat of violence within the scope of household and community.
14. Facilitator is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide handling and protection for Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that provides Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the district and village/sub-district level that provides protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from disturbance of psychosocial condition and restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and facing difficulties in legal matters outside or before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and their child, or mother and their child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relations due to blood relation, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 3

The objectives of implementing protection of Victims are:

a. to prevent Violence Against Women and Children; b. to provide services to women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. to empower women and Child Victims of Violence.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as the element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries and is authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Sub-district is a district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the duties of the district head.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, court, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of Victims of violence to be able to work and be self-sufficient after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any action against women that results or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is women and Children who experience violence and/or threat of violence within the scope of household and community.
14. Facilitator is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide handling and protection for Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that provides Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the district and village/sub-district level that provides protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from disturbance of psychosocial condition and restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and facing difficulties in legal matters outside or before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and their child, or mother and their child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relations due to blood relation, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.

15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide handling and protection for Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.

17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the district and village/sub-district level that provides protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from disturbance of psychosocial condition and restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and facing difficulties in legal matters outside or before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.

22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and their child, or mother and their child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relations due to blood relation, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.

26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Point a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, group, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, compatible and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances to access, participate, control and benefit from the implementation of development and enjoy the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Point e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death occurring during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions

Point f.

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g

What is meant by "respect for the opinion of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h

What is meant by "openness" is that the implementation of victim protection is transparent among integrated service providers.

Point i

What is meant by "integration" is that the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, religious leaders, social workers, police.

Point j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence they experienced.

Point k

What is meant by "empowering" is every effort provided must strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Point l

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of the victim to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 17

Point a

Point b

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE Part One

General

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 23

(1) Forms of fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Violence include the fulfillment of Children's basic rights according to their needs.

(2) The fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is the responsibility of the Regional Government, family, and community.

Article 11

(1) In an effort to enhance protection for Victims of violence, UPPA is established at the sub-district and Village/Sub-district levels.

(2) UPPA at the sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by the Sub-district Head by involving community institutions, the Sub-district Level Family Welfare Development Task Force, community leaders and Child representatives.

(3) UPPA at the Village/Sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by the Village Head/Sub-district Head by involving Village/Sub-district officials, community institutions in the Village/Sub-district, the Family Welfare Development Task Force, community leaders and Child representatives.

(4) UPPA as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to provide protection to Victims in the form of:

a. pursuing prevention and handling;
b. conducting coordination in the framework of handling services for Victims of Violence;
c. pursuing increased community participation; and d. conducting monitoring and reporting.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Blora Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as the element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries and is authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Sub-district is a district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the duties of the district head.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, court, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of Victims of violence to be able to work and be self-sufficient after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any action against women that results or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is women and Children who experience violence and/or threat of violence within the scope of household and community.
14. Facilitator is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide handling and protection for Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that provides Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the district and village/sub-district level that provides protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from disturbance of psychosocial condition and restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and facing difficulties in legal matters outside or before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and their child, or mother and their child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relations due to blood relation, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Point a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, group, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, compatible and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances to access, participate, control and benefit from the implementation of development and enjoy the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Point e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death occurring during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions

Point f.

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g

What is meant by "respect for the opinion of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h

What is meant by "openness" is that the implementation of victim protection is transparent among integrated service providers.

Point i

What is meant by "integration" is that the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, religious leaders, social workers, police.

Point j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence they experienced.

Point k

What is meant by "empowering" is every effort provided must strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Point l

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of the victim to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

CHAPTER VIII

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE Part One

General

Article 17

Point a

What is meant by "fast" is immediate action taken without complications or simplified procedures.

Point b

What is meant by "safe and comfortable" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, undisturbed, and served in a friendly, respectful and appreciative manner.

Point c

What is meant by "empathy" is an act of appreciating, respecting, caring, being friendly, and making happy with the aim of pleasing and calming the victim's heart.

Point d

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is service to women and children victims of violence without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point e

What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people regardless of their social status, so that such services are affordable for the underprivileged or relatively affordable for the privileged.

Point f

What is meant by "not subject to fees" is that service and assistance activities conducted by PPT are not charged to victims.

Point g

What is meant by "guaranteed confidentiality" is an effort to ensure certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection towards Victims includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts towards Victims of Violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Blora Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as the element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries and is authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Sub-district is a district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the duties of the district head.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, court, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of Victims of violence to be able to work and be self-sufficient after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any action against women that results or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is women and Children who experience violence and/or threat of violence within the scope of household and community.
14. Facilitator is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide handling and protection for Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that provides Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the district and village/sub-district level that provides protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from disturbance of psychosocial condition and restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and facing difficulties in legal matters outside or before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and their child, or mother and their child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relations due to blood relation, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

Article 14

The organization of protection for Victims of Violence is carried out through: a. prevention efforts;

b. services; and

c. empowerment.

Article 11

(1) In an effort to enhance protection for Victims of violence, UPPA is established at the sub-district and Village/Sub-district levels.

(2) UPPA at the sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by the Sub-district Head by involving community institutions, the Sub-district Level Family Welfare Development Task Force, community leaders and Child representatives.

(3) UPPA at the Village/Sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by the Village Head/Sub-district Head by involving Village/Sub-district officials, community institutions in the Village/Sub-district, the Family Welfare Development Task Force, community leaders and Child representatives.

(4) UPPA as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to provide protection to Victims in the form of:

a. pursuing prevention and handling;
b. conducting coordination in the framework of handling services for Victims of Violence;
c. pursuing increased community participation; and d. conducting monitoring and reporting.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

Article 2

Point a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, group, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, compatible and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances to access, participate, control and benefit from the implementation of development and enjoy the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Point e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death occurring during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions

Point f.

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g

What is meant by "respect for the opinion of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h

What is meant by "openness" is that the implementation of victim protection is transparent among integrated service providers.

Point i

What is meant by "integration" is that the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, religious leaders, social workers, police.

Point j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence they experienced.

Point k

What is meant by "empowering" is every effort provided must strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Point l

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of the victim to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

3.2.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Blora Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as the element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries and is authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Sub-district is a district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the duties of the district head.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, court, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of Victims of violence to be able to work and be self-sufficient after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any action against women that results or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is women and Children who experience violence and/or threat of violence within the scope of household and community.
14. Facilitator is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide handling and protection for Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that provides Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the district and village/sub-district level that provides protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from disturbance of psychosocial condition and restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and facing difficulties in legal matters outside or before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and their child, or mother and their child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relations due to blood relation, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore need to be protected in terms of dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection towards Victims includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts towards Victims of Violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Blora Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as the element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries and is authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Sub-district is a district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the duties of the district head.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, court, or other parties either temporarily or based on court order.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of Victims of violence to be able to work and be self-sufficient after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any action against women that results or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is women and Children who experience violence and/or threat of violence within the scope of household and community.
14. Facilitator is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide handling and protection for Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that provides Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the district and village/sub-district level that provides protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from disturbance of psychosocial condition and restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and facing difficulties in legal matters outside or before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and their child, or mother and their child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relations due to blood relation, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

Article 2

Point a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, group, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, compatible and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances to access, participate, control and benefit from the implementation of development and enjoy the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Point e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death occurring during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions

Point f.

What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g

What is meant by "respect for the opinion of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h

What is meant by "openness" is that the implementation of victim protection is transparent among integrated service providers.

Point i

What is meant by "integration" is that the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, religious leaders, social workers, police.

Point j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence they experienced.

Point k

What is meant by "empowering" is every effort provided must strengthen the victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Point l

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of the victim to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.
